subject: English Language
title: Tenses
introduction: Choose the right time and verb form, then practise five questions at a time.

rules.title: Simple: facts, habits and finished actions
rules.body: Simple present describes habits and facts; simple past describes completed past events; simple future uses will + base verb. Check time clues such as every day, yesterday and tomorrow.
rules.example: She walks every day. · She walked yesterday. · She will walk tomorrow.

rules.title: Continuous: action in progress
rules.body: Use am/is/are + -ing now, was/were + -ing at a past time, and will be + -ing at a future time. Match the helping verb to the subject.
rules.example: She is reading. · They were reading. · He will be reading.

rules.title: Perfect: action completed by a point
rules.body: Present perfect uses has/have + past participle; past perfect uses had + participle for an earlier past action; future perfect uses will have + participle before a future deadline.
rules.example: She has finished. · She had finished before noon. · She will have finished by Friday.

rules.title: Perfect continuous and time clues
rules.body: For an action continuing over time use has/have been, had been or will have been + -ing. Since marks a starting point; for marks a duration.
rules.example: He has been waiting since noon. · They had been playing for an hour.

worked.prompt: By Friday, they ___ the project. (finish; future perfect)
worked.explanation: By Friday gives a future deadline, so use will have + finished.

questions.prompt: 1.The children are decorating the classroom for the competition.(Simple Past)
questions.answer: The children decorated the classroom for the competition.
questions.explanation: Simple past uses the past form decorated.

questions.prompt:
The chef prepares fresh bread every morning.
(Past Continuous)
questions.answer: The chef was preparing fresh bread that morning.
accepted: The chef was preparing fresh bread every morning.
questions.explanation: Past continuous uses was preparing. A specific past time sounds more natural than every morning.

questions.prompt:
The mechanic repaired the damaged bicycle.
(Present Continuous)
questions.answer: The mechanic is repairing the damaged bicycle.
questions.explanation: Present continuous uses is repairing.

questions.prompt:
The students have submitted their projects to the teacher.
(Past Perfect)
questions.answer: The students had submitted their projects to the teacher.
questions.explanation: Past perfect uses had submitted.

questions.prompt:
The farmer harvested the wheat from the field.
(Present Perfect)
questions.answer: The farmer has harvested the wheat from the field.
questions.explanation: Present perfect uses has harvested.

questions.prompt: The workers have been painting the school building since Monday.(Simple Past)
questions.answer: The workers painted the school building.
questions.explanation: Simple past uses painted.

questions.prompt:
The doctor examines every patient carefully.
(Future Continuous)
questions.answer: The doctor will be examining every patient carefully.
questions.explanation: Future continuous uses will be examining.

questions.prompt: The train will leave the station at six o'clock tomorrow morning.(Future Perfect)
questions.answer: The train will have left the station by six o'clock tomorrow morning.
accepted: The train will have left the station at six o'clock tomorrow morning.
questions.explanation: Future perfect uses will have left. By states a deadline; the worksheet key changes at to by.

questions.prompt: The musician was practising the piano when the lights went out. (Present Perfect Continuous)
questions.answer: The musician has been practising the piano since morning.
accepted: The musician has been practising the piano since the lights went out.
questions.explanation: Present perfect continuous uses has been practising. Since the lights went out can preserve the original time event.

questions.prompt: 1. She _____ to the market before it started raining.
questions.explanation: Past perfect shows she had gone before the rain started; simple past is also grammatical here.

questions.prompt: 2. Which of the following sentences uses the simple present tense correctly?

options.text: (a) I conduct yoga classes every morning.
(b) I conducted yoga classes every semester.
(c) I will be conducting yoga classes in the new school.

questions.explanation: A habitual action uses the simple present.

questions.prompt: 3. They ____ football every Sunday.
questions.explanation: Every Sunday signals a habit.

questions.prompt: 4. I cannot go out to play because I ______ my homework now.
questions.explanation: Now signals an action in progress.

questions.prompt: 5.  Riti _____ to Paris next summer.
questions.explanation: Both will go and is going can describe a future trip; is going often suggests an arrangement.

questions.prompt: 6. By next year, she ________ her degree.
questions.explanation: By next year points to completion before a future time.

questions.prompt: 11.Ram and Shyam ______ in the garden right now.
questions.explanation: Right now calls for the present continuous.

questions.prompt: (a) My friend _____ (dance) on stage yesterday. (simple past)
questions.explanation: Use the tense named in brackets and agree with the subject.

questions.prompt:
(b) The government _______ (impose) a fine on tax defaulters.
         (future continuous)
questions.explanation: Use the tense named in brackets and agree with the subject.

questions.prompt: (c) Geography ____ (be) best understood with an atlas. (simple present)
questions.explanation: Use the tense named in brackets and agree with the subject.

questions.prompt: (d) We ______ (visit) the museum twice before it closed last year. (past perfect)
questions.explanation: Use the tense named in brackets and agree with the subject.

questions.prompt: (e) The company ________ (work) on the product launch. (simple future)
questions.explanation: Use the tense named in brackets and agree with the subject.

questions.prompt: By the time we arrived, the play ___. (already begin; past perfect)
questions.explanation: The earlier past action uses had + past participle.

questions.prompt: She ___ for an hour when the rain began. (read; past perfect continuous)
questions.explanation: An action continuing before a past event uses had been + -ing.

questions.prompt: I ___ my homework when you called. (do; past continuous)
questions.explanation: An ongoing past action uses was or were + -ing.

questions.prompt: By Friday, they ___ the project. (finish; future perfect)
questions.explanation: Future perfect uses will have + past participle.

questions.prompt: He ___ here since 2021. (live; present perfect continuous)
questions.explanation: Since marks the start of an action continuing now.

questions.prompt: The train usually ___ at six. (leave; simple present)
questions.explanation: A timetable or habit uses simple present.

questions.prompt: Listen! Someone ___ at the door. (knock; present continuous)
questions.explanation: Listen signals something happening now.

questions.prompt: They ___ the match before the storm began. (win; past perfect)
questions.explanation: The win happened before another past event.

questions.prompt: We ___ our cousins next weekend. (visit; simple future)
questions.explanation: Will + base verb forms the simple future.

questions.prompt: The children ___ when the teacher entered. (talk; past continuous)
questions.explanation: A past action in progress uses were + -ing.

questions.prompt: She ___ her keys, so she cannot open the door. (lose; present perfect)
questions.explanation: A past event with a present result uses present perfect.
